questions.question_text: Factorise $-15x^2-25x$ by taking out a negative HCF.

options.why: Did not flip the second sign; $-25x\div -5x=+5$, so the constant inside is positive.
Took out a positive $5x$, which expands to $15x^2+25x$ — the opposite sign of the original.
Forgot to divide the second term's coefficient by $5$, leaving $25$ instead of $5$.

questions.question_text: Factorise $14y-21y^2$ by taking out a negative HCF.

options.why: Divided by $-7y$ but kept the original signs; $14y\div -7y=-2$, not $+2$.
Kept the minus from $-21y^2$ instead of dividing it by the negative factor to get $+3y$.
Did not subtract the indices: $-21y^2\div -7y=3y$, not $3y^2$.
Did not carry the minus sign on the last term; $-21cd^2\div 7cd=-3d$.
Divided $14cd$ by $7$ only, leaving $2cd$ instead of $2$ inside the brackets.
Did not reduce the index on the first term; $7c^2d\div 7cd=c$, not $c^2$.

questions.question_text: The expression $3(10a-15a^2+20ab)$ is not fully factorised. Which is the fully factorised form?

options.why: Did not divide the last term by $a$; $20ab\div 5a=4b$, not $4ab$.
Added the two factors $3$ and $5$ instead of multiplying them to get $15$.
Lost the minus sign on the middle term when the extra factor $5a$ was taken out.

questions.question_text: Which pair shows $-6k+18k^2$ factorised with a positive HCF and then with a negative HCF?

options.why: The second form takes out the negative but leaves the signs unflipped, so it expands to $6k-18k^2$.
The first form has both signs reversed, expanding to $6k-18k^2$ instead of the original.
Only the first sign was flipped in the negative form; $18k^2\div -6k=-3k$.

questions.question_text: Which of these expressions is **not** fully factorised?

options.why: $2$ and $3$ share no common factor and no pronumeral is common, so this is fully factorised.
$1$ and $2$ share no common factor and no pronumeral is common, so this is fully factorised.
$4$ and $5$ share no common factor and no pronumeral is common, so this is fully factorised.

questions.solution_text:
$4(3a-6b)$
$= 4 \times 3(a-2b)$
$= 12(a-2b)$
The terms $3a$ and $-6b$ still share a factor of $3$, so $4(3a-6b)$ is not fully factorised.

questions.question_text: Factorise $-8x^3y+12x^2y^2-20x^2y$ by taking out a negative HCF.

options.why: Did not flip the last sign; $-20x^2y\div -4x^2y=+5$.
Did not flip the middle sign; $12x^2y^2\div -4x^2y=-3y$.
Did not subtract the indices on the first term; $-8x^3y\div -4x^2y=2x$, not $2x^2$.
